key_insight: The paper develops dimension-efficient neural network approximations for fractional parabolic PDEs by introducing anisotropic spectral Barron spaces that separately control time and space regularity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable theory for approximating time-dependent fractional diffusion models with lower-order drift and potential terms, which is relevant for high-dimensional scientific computing.
method: Define anisotropic spectral Barron norms in space-time Fourier variables to capture temporal and spatial smoothness separately.
Prove dimension-independent maximal regularity using multiplication estimates plus the method of continuity for lower-order terms.
Use a Vandermonde-based global-in-time extension of the fractional heat semigroup to analyze forward evolution and derive network approximation bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical approximation results, including n^{-1/2} two-layer bounds in mixed Sobolev norms under stated regularity assumptions.
watch_item: The uniform-in-time spectral Barron regularity can fail, so the theory depends on carefully chosen anisotropic regularity assumptions and may not apply to all solutions.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation of Solutions to Fractional Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
